system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo
T3: Adding Kubernetes, AWS, MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, SageMaker) because ML ads list them
T4: Mistranslating employer or degree (Mag. ing. comp. is a master's degree)
T5: Writing the English output with Croatian section headings or leaving Croatian text untranslated
T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 1: CV
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP & Document AI
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience across NLP, data science and research,
including deploying machine learning systems to production. Specialised in document classification and
named entity recognition for Croatian administrative text. Experienced in taking models from dataset
preparation and experimentation through model serving and production monitoring, using Python,
MLflow and Azure. Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science focused on Croatian-language NLP.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
• Developed and deployed a classifier for scanned incoming public-administration documents,
achieving 94% accuracy and 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes; the service processes approximately
15,000 documents per day.
• Fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić transformer models for document classification and named entity
recognition in Croatian administrative text, including persons, organisations, OIB numbers,
addresses and legal references.
• Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 documents and developed annotation guidelines; achieved an
inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.
• Implemented model serving with FastAPI and Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and
MLflow for experimentation and model registry.
• Established weekly production monitoring for text length, vocabulary and predicted-class
distribution, with alerts for PSI above 0.2. Detected a client-side OCR change associated with a
9-point accuracy drop and helped resolve it within a week.
• Mentor two student interns.
Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021–02/2023
• Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales
team.
• Built a customer complaint topic-classification workflow for customer-service reporting, progressing
from TF-IDF and logistic regression to fastText; classified 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer
service management.
• Prepared SQL reports from an Oracle data warehouse.
Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava |
10/2020–08/2021
• Created a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated data; wrote supporting Python scripts.
SELECTED PROJECT
Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project 2025
• Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using a sentence-embedding
model, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
• Prototype only; not used in production and checked manually without formal evaluation.
EDUCATION
PhD studies in Computer Science | University of Drava 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts | Expected completion: 2027
MSc in Computer Science (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava 2020
CERTIFICATIONS & TEACHING
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024
Guest Lecturer, NLP Summer School | 2025 (90-minute lecture)
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, SQL, pandas, NumPy
Machine learning and NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM,
fastText, spaCy, sentence-transformers, TF-IDF
Production ML and MLOps: MLflow, model registry, FastAPI model serving, Docker, Azure ML,
Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently, production monitoring, data-drift monitoring
Data and tools: Oracle SQL, PostgreSQL, FAISS, Label Studio, Git, Linux
LANGUAGES
Croatian: Native | English: C1 (regular English-language client meetings) | German: B2
PUBLICATION
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). “Named Entity Recognition for Croatian Administrative Documents.”
Regional workshop on Slavic language processing.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I hold an MSc in
Computer Science and work primarily in Python. I bring more than five years of experience across
machine learning, NLP and research, including deploying models into production, and I am
particularly interested in applying this experience to systems that help support teams respond to
customers efficiently.
In my current role as a Machine Learning Engineer at Slavonica Document AI, I develop NLP
systems for Croatian administrative documents. I built and deployed a document classifier that
handles approximately 15,000 documents per day, and fine-tuned transformer models for
classification and named entity recognition. I also implemented model serving with FastAPI and
Docker on Azure, used Azure ML and MLflow for experimentation, model registry and MLOps
workflows, and established production monitoring that helped detect and resolve an OCR change
associated with a nine-point accuracy drop. This work has given me experience carrying models
from data preparation and experimentation through serving and ongoing operation.
Earlier, as a Data Scientist at Baranjska kreditna banka, I built a customer-complaint
topic-classification workflow, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic-regression baseline to
fastText. The resulting 11-topic classification supported weekly reporting to customer-service
management. I also built a personal retrieval-augmented question-answering prototype over
Croatian laws using sentence-transformers, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an
API; it was a manually checked weekend prototype rather than a production system. I am also
pursuing a PhD in computer science focused on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.
Together, these experiences have shaped my practical approach to language-focused ML, from
preparing text data to building and monitoring useful systems.
Quillstone’s focus on AI for customer operations is a strong match for my background in NLP,
customer-support text classification and production ML systems. I am drawn to the team’s
ownership, pragmatic approach and emphasis on learning from mistakes—principles that fit well
with the careful monitoring and iterative improvement required for production ML. I would
welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your AI team.
Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
